<!-- pr-reviewer: 8d5cbe8b92fbbe72b6d8fc92bb9ea104c71f4d70 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The routing fix is right and I confirmed it end to end, posted output included. One small pin is missing: the Post page's "where a pick lands" line has no test.

Reviewed under the safety tier, because a wrong machine or post means wrong posted G-code and wrong limits.

### What looks good
- The root cause is fixed in one place. `route_machine` and `choose_post` now ask `machine_target()` / `post_target()` (`crates/ui/src/state_setup_mount.rs:51-69`). Every GUI machine verb goes through `route_machine`: library combo, Load other, Edit apply, Clear, Machines pane "Use for this setup", and the ribbon mode switch (`machine_modes.rs:73` pushes `LoadBuiltinMachine`). I grepped `crates/ui/src`, and no other GUI path builds `LoadMachine` / `SelectPost`.
- Undo is real. Each pick is one `SetSetupMachine` / `SetSetupPost`, and its `invert` gives the previous owner back (the setup follows the document again).
- Single-setup documents are unchanged. `shared_mount_target` needs `names().len() > 1`. Mutating it to `> 0` or `> 2` both fail pins.
- The page line is honest about the active setup. `ownership` only draws for the active setup (`setup_pages.rs:77-83`, `editable`), so comparing the target with `name` is sound.
- An own "no machine" (Clear on Setup2) survives a save and load. `SetupMachineDto` with `machine` absent means "deliberately no machine" (`crates/app/src/project/mount_dto.rs:14-22`), so the setup does not quietly fall back to the document's machine.
- The decision record, provenance lines and conventional subject are in place. No process files, `CHANGELOG.md` or snapshot PNGs are touched. All files stay under ~400 lines.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream/main 41cd9c2, clean merge)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-ui --lib`, single-threaded, CWD `crates/ui` | 716 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| ui suites from the gate plan: boundary 3, boundary_picks 6, feedback 6, fixtures 7, gpu_render 11 (+1 ignored), machine 6, models 4, operations 31, shell 20, sinker_setup 1, theme_files 14 | all pass |
| app: setup_mount 6, setup_mounts_post 8, setup_mount_trace 6, mcp_setup_mount_trace 3, mcp_setup 9, commands_undo 30, project_roundtrip 73, setup_post_options 10 | all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**End-to-end posting check.** This was a local scratch test, not pushed. It builds the GUI `State` with a VMC document and per-setup Face ops, runs the GUI commands, generates, then calls `posting::post_mounts`:
- **Two setups, Setup2 picks Tormach 770M through `LoadBuiltinMachine`.** Two files. `job_01_Setup1.nc` starts `O0001 (VMC 3-AXIS)` and has Face1/G54. `job_02_Setup2.nc` starts `O0001 (Tormach 770M)` and has Face2/G55. Limits per setup: Setup1 has spindle 50-12000 rpm and 7.5 kW; Setup2 has 175-10000 rpm and 1.1 kW. After undo the setup follows the document again and the job posts one file.
- **Three setups, Setup2 picks the 770M plus the Siemens 840D post.** `job_01_Setup1_Setup3.nc` is VMC/Fanuc with Face1 and Face3 and no G710. `job_02_Setup2.nc` is `; Tormach 770M`, `N10 G17 G710 ... G55`, Face2 only.
- **One setup, picks of the 770M and Haas.** Both still land on the document (no own mount). One file, 770M.
- **Setup1 owns a Lathe, then Setup2 picks the 770M.** Setup1 keeps its Lathe and the document keeps its VMC. Setup2's "use the document's machine" and its undo walk correctly.

**Mutation checks** (each reverted; scored against the PR's own `setup_machine_bleed` + `setup_mount_pages` pins):
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `machine_target` owner-only | 3 fail |
| `route_machine` matches `machine_owner()` | 3 fail |
| `choose_post` matches `post_owner()` | 1 fails (`a_post_picked_on_setup2_leaves_setup1s_post`) |
| `shared_mount_target` `> 1` changed to `> 0` | 3 fail |
| `shared_mount_target` `> 1` changed to `> 2` | 4 fail |
| page line forced "own" / forced "document" / removed | 1 / 1 / 2 fail |
| **`setup_pages.rs:128` `Mount::Post => state.post_target()` changed to `state.machine_target()`** | **0 fail (survives)** |

### Requested before merge
1. **Pin the Post page's target line** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_pages.rs:126-129`). Every PR test reads the Machine page, so the `Mount::Post` arm is unpinned. It shows a real wrong statement: with one setup that owns its machine but follows the document's post, the mutated page says "A post picked on this page is Setup1's own" while a pick actually sets the document's post. A test of about 10 lines closes it, and I checked that it fails under the mutation: one setup, `SetupOwnMachine { setup: "Setup1", own: true }`, open `SetupNode("Setup1", SetupPage::Post)`, then assert `query_by_label(&target_line("post", "Setup1", false))` is present.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **MCP parity is by design, not identical behaviour.** `load_machine` without `setup` in a two-setup document still writes the document's machine, which every following setup reads. The decision record argues this well: the agent names its target explicitly. A one-line note in the `camcraft-mcp` skill ("without `setup`, every setup that follows the document moves") could help agents, perhaps alongside #1526.
- **No GUI route sets the document's machine in a 2+ setup document.** The decision record already says this ("Cost to change later"). The radio still shows "Use the document's machine (X)" for a value the user can no longer change from any page. Worth a follow-up issue if users ask for it.
- Post OPTIONS still route to the document. That is #1526, stacked next, as the body says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 40f461fe4fb1bf2e408878a444d69970b123fa63 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (delta re-review of 8d5cbe8b..40f461fe)

**What looks good**
- The delta is test-only: one new test in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_machine_bleed.rs` (+21 lines), no product code.
- It closes the earlier blocker. With `setup_pages.rs:128` mutated to `Mount::Post => state.machine_target()`, `a_setup_owning_only_its_machine_names_the_documents_post_on_its_post_page` **fails**. With the line restored it passes. The pin also asserts the negative case (the label never names the machine's own target).

**Local results (merged with current main, the merge was clean)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| mutation `Mount::Post => machine_target()` | new pin FAILS (expected) |
| restored, new pin | 1 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib`, `--test-threads=1`, CWD `crates/ui` | 721 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
- None.

**Notes**
- The stacked #1535 (reviewed clean at 6bd49fd9) needs a merge of main after this PR merges.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
